Description: Materialized access-log table. Contains one row per facility access event (gate/door entry attempts), enriched with contact, facility, and organisation context. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The access code entered for the entry attempt.
The tenant who triggered the access event. Joins to contact.contact_id.
Timestamp when the record was created in the system.
The name of the access control device (e.g., gate keypad, door reader).
The type of access event (e.g., entry, exit).
The facility where the event occurred. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
Name of the facility where the event occurred. Denormalized from facilities.
Unique identifier for the access log entry.
Timestamp when the access event occurred.
The organization identifier. Common filter field across all views.
Name of the organization that owns the facility. Denormalized.
Additional detail about the result, particularly for denied access attempts.
The outcome of the access attempt (e.g., granted, denied).
Timestamp when the record was last updated.

Materialized AI-call-outcomes table. Contains one row per call leg answered by the AI voice agent (Patty), with what the agent got done: leads and leases created, move-outs scheduled, and handoffs to staff or the payment line. Only outcome flags are included; the agent's prompts, model usage and tool-call logs are not. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The call leg the AI agent answered. Primary key. Joins to call_child.call_child_id.
How long the AI agent was on the call, in seconds.
The parent call. Joins to calls.call_id.
Timestamp when the outcome was recorded, in facility local time.
The facility the call was for. Joins to facilities.facility_id. NULL for calls to an organization-wide number that were not tied to a facility.
The facility name. Denormalized.
The team the AI agent handed the call to: GENERAL, SALES, OPS or PAYMENT. NULL when there was no handoff, and for calls before this was recorded.
Whether the AI agent handed the caller to a person.
Whether the AI agent created a lead during the call.
Whether the AI agent created a lease during the call.
Whether the AI agent scheduled a move-out during the call.
Whether the AI agent handed the caller to the secure payment line.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
Timestamp when the outcome was last updated, in facility local time.
How the call ended: PATTY_REQUESTED (the AI agent ended it), REMOTE_PARTICIPANT (the caller hung up), TRANSFER (it was handed off) or UNKNOWN. NULL for calls before this was recorded.

Materialized auctions table. Contains one row per auction event (typically lien auctions for delinquent tenants) with facility and organisation attribution. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The deadline by which the auction must be advertised, as required by lien law.
Unique identifier for the auction.
Timestamp when the auction record was created.
Scheduled date and time of the auction.
The facility hosting the auction. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
Name of the facility hosting the auction. Denormalized from facilities.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
Timestamp when the auction record was last updated.

Materialized book-entry table. Contains one row per accounting book entry (charges, payments, credits, and transfers), enriched with facility, lease, unit, and contact context. External ID (user_...) of the manager/user who created the journal entry. May be absent from managers, which lists only the org's own managers (e.g., Cubby call-center staff are not included). NULL when added_by is NULL.
The monetary amount of the entry.
Portion allocated to assets on the balance sheet.
Portion allocated to liabilities.
Portion of the amount allocated to payments received.
Portion of the amount allocated to revenue.
Portion allocated to transfers between accounts.
References another entry this one applies to (e.g., a payment applying against a specific charge).
Categorizes the entry within accounts receivable (e.g., rent, fees, insurance).
The accounting book/ledger this entry belongs to (e.g., A/R).

The tenant/contact for this entry. Joins to contact.contact_id.
The tenant's name. Denormalized from contact.
Lease discount this entry is attributed to, where applicable. Joins to discounts.discount_id.
The datetime of the accounting entry.
Sequential entry number within a transaction.
Short code or label describing the entry type.

Description of the journal entry this entry belongs to, as shown on the ledger.

Materialized call-agent-availability table. Aggregates manager status durations by day and status for call-center availability reporting. The date for which availability is recorded, in the organization's call-center time zone (see time_zone).

Materialized call-center-reservations table. Contains one row each time the call-center queue offered a call to an agent, with the queue, the agent, whether they accepted it, and any transfer. A call that rings several agents has several rows. Only organizations using Cubby's call-center queue have rows. Timestamps are in facility local time; for calls not tied to a facility, they are in the organization's call-center time zone. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
Timestamp when the agent accepted the call, in facility local time. NULL if never accepted.
Unique identifier for the offer. Primary key.
The call leg that was offered. Joins to call_child.call_child_id.
The parent call. Joins to calls.call_id. NULL when the call could not be linked.
Timestamp when the row was created, in facility local time.
INBOUND or OUTBOUND. NULL for the few offers whose queue task was not recorded.
Why the offer ended, as reported by the call-center system (for example 'All reservations were completed' or 'hangup'). Often NULL.
Timestamp when the offer ended, in facility local time.
The facility the call was for. Joins to facilities.facility_id. NULL for calls not tied to a facility.
The facility name. Denormalized.
The agent the call was offered to. Joins to managers.manager_id.
The agent's name. Denormalized.
Timestamp when the call was offered to the agent, in facility local time.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
The call-center queue the call was waiting in, as set up for the organization.

What happened to the offer: COMPLETED (accepted and finished), TIMEOUT (not answered in time), REJECTED (declined by the agent), CANCELED (the call left the queue before the agent answered, for example because the caller hung up), RESCINDED (withdrawn, for example because another agent took the call), or ACCEPTED, WRAPPING or OFFERED while still in progress.
The agent's team (manager group) at the time of the offer.
The agent who transferred the call. Joins to managers.manager_id. NULL when not a transfer.
The transferring agent's name. Denormalized.
For a call this agent was transferred, COLD (transferred without introduction) or WARM (introduced first). NULL when not a transfer.
Timestamp when the transfer started, in facility local time. NULL when not a transfer.
For a transfer, whether it completed, failed, was canceled or is still initiated. NULL when not a transfer.
Timestamp when the row was last updated, in facility local time.
Timestamp when the call ended and the agent started wrap-up, in facility local time. NULL if never accepted.

Materialized call-child table. Contains one row per child call interaction — a single inbound call may have multiple legs (e.g., IVR, transfer to agent). Enriched with abandonment logic, facility context, assigned manager details, and a customer-facing call script with recorded Patty action telemetry. Use for granular call routing and agent-level analysis. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
Whether the caller hung up before the call was answered by an agent (true/false)
The type of agent handling this leg (e.g., human, bot/IVR).
Timestamp when this leg was answered.
Unique identifier for the child call leg.
The parent call this leg belongs to. Joins to calls.call_id.

Customer-facing script-style rendering of the call leg. Contains a [CALL METADATA] line, an optional [TRANSCRIPT] status line, timed [MM:SS] or [HH:MM:SS] Caller/Patty dialogue lines for Patty calls when transcription is available, and a final [RECORDED PATTY ACTIONS] line sourced from recorded Patty action telemetry.
Whether this leg is inbound or outbound.
Duration in milliseconds of this call leg.
The facility associated with this call leg. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
The facility name. Denormalized from facilities.
TRUE when a recording is stored for this call leg (same rule the app uses for its hasRecording flag). Open it in the manager app at /calls/records/{call_id}.
The manager who handled this leg, if human. Joins to managers.manager_id.
The manager's name. Denormalized.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
Timestamp when the parent call started. Denormalized from calls.started_at.
JSON object containing AI-scored quality metrics for this call leg.
Timestamp when this specific leg started.
Outcome/status of this call leg (e.g., answered, no-answer, transferred).
JSON object containing the transcription of this call leg.
Seconds the caller waited before this leg was answered.

Matches the app API: exemptions that were removed, replaced or have expired are not included. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The tenant on the lease. Joins to contacts.contact_id.
Timestamp when the exemption was created, in facility local time.
Unique identifier for the exemption. Primary key.
The date the exemption ends, as entered. Can briefly be in the past until the app's expiry job removes the exemption.
The facility of the lease. Joins to facilities.facility_id.
The facility name. Denormalized.
Whether automated collections messages to the tenant are paused.
Whether late and delinquency fees are paused for this lease.
Whether the lease is held back from becoming lien-eligible (the path to auction).
Whether the overlock step is paused for this lease.

The organization identifier. Common filter field.
Free-text explanation, required when reason is OTHER. NULL otherwise.

Materialized value-pricing-strategy-tiers table. Contains one row per tier (LOWEST, MEDIUM, HIGHEST) of each value pricing strategy: the tiered rate options offered at online checkout, with each tier's name, price increase and listed benefits. Join to pricing_group on value_pricing_strategy_id to see which unit types use a strategy, and to leads.value_pricing_tier to see which tier a prospect picked. Timestamps are in America/New_York because a strategy belongs to the organization, not a facility. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The benefits listed for the tier at checkout, separated by '|'.
Timestamp when the tier was created, in America/New_York time.
The dollar or percentage increase over the web rate. NULL for the LOWEST tier.
How the tier's price is set from the unit's web rate: DOLLAR (adds increase_amount) or PERCENTAGE (adds increase_amount percent). NULL for the LOWEST tier, which is always the web rate.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.
The tier: LOWEST, MEDIUM or HIGHEST. Matches leads.value_pricing_tier.

What happens when a tier has no unit available: FILL_ALL_TIERS (offer a unit from the nearest tier that has one, in either direction), FILL_LOWER_TIERS (only offer a unit from the tier above, so a cheaper option stays available) or NONE (no unit is borrowed from another tier).
The tier's customer-facing name, such as Good, Better or Best.
Timestamp when the tier was last updated, in America/New_York time.
The value pricing strategy. Joins to pricing_group.value_pricing_strategy_id. Together with tier, the primary key.
The strategy's name as set up in Cubby. Matches pricing_group.value_pricing_strategy_name.

Materialized workflow-runs table. Contains one row per run of an automated workflow (a sequence of texts, emails and tasks that starts when a lease goes overdue, a lead or reservation is created, or a move-in or move-out is created), with the lease or lead that started it and how far it got. Emails, sms and tasks sent by a run carry its workflow_run_id. Row-level security enforced via a BigQuery Row Access Policy on org_id. Published atomically from an RLS-protected staging table so the previous protected version remains available until cutover; see includes/refresh.js.
The tenant or prospect on that lease or lead. Joins to contacts.contact_id.
Timestamp when the run started, in facility local time.
The facility of that lease or lead. Joins to facilities.facility_id. NULL for leads not tied to a facility.
The facility name. Denormalized.
The lead that started the run. Joins to leads.lead_id. Set for LEAD_CREATED and RESERVATION_CREATED runs; NULL if the lead has since been deleted.
The lease that started the run. Joins to leases.lease_id. Set for ACCOUNT_OVERDUE, MOVE_IN_CREATED and MOVE_OUT_CREATED runs; NULL if the lease has since been deleted.
The organization identifier. Common filter field.

RUNNING (still in progress), COMPLETED (finished every step), STOPPED (ended early, for example because the tenant paid, the lead was closed, the tenant moved out, a stop condition was met or a manager stopped it) or FAILED.
How many of the workflow's steps the run has finished. For a COMPLETED run this is every step.
What started the run: ACCOUNT_OVERDUE, MOVE_IN_CREATED or MOVE_OUT_CREATED (for a lease), or LEAD_CREATED or RESERVATION_CREATED (for a lead).
Timestamp when the run last advanced or changed status, in facility local time. For a run that is no longer RUNNING, this is normally when it ended.
The workflow that ran.
The workflow's name as set up in Cubby.
Unique identifier for the run. Primary key. Joins to emails.workflow_run_id, sms.workflow_run_id and tasks.workflow_run_id.
Whether the workflow is currently PUBLISHED (starting new runs) or UNPUBLISHED. This is the workflow's state now, not when the run started.
The version of the workflow the run followed. Runs keep the version they started on when the workflow is later edited.
